title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain Treg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.
authors: Huang Wenjun; Li Jun; He Minghong; Xu Beisi; Rosikiewicz Wojciech et al.
abstract: Regulatory T cells (Treg cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by Treg cells versus conventional T cells (Tconv cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS-trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports Treg cell development and function. Although Wdr82 deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell-specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory Tconv cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type Treg cells, indicating a primary defect in Treg cell-mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at Treg cell-associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the Treg cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains Treg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

title: Anticipate, acclimate, recuperate, and remember: how spatiotemporal signal integration controls flooding stress resilience in plants.
authors: Rodriguez-Cisneros Carlos; Agashe Advait; Chaudhury Rim; Daniel Kevin; Hewedy Omar A et al.
abstract: Flooding is a major abiotic stress that restricts terrestrial plant growth and survival. A plant tissue's ability to avoid or sustain critical oxygen deprivation (hypoxia) and subsequent re-oxygenation damage is vital for its survival. Submergence triggers rapid ethylene and hypoxia signalling that in turn control acclimation responses, promoting plant resilience. Interestingly, an extensive range of additional environmental and internal factors were shown to influence these canonical signalling pathways associated with flooding acclimation and tolerance. Here, we discuss how such integrative ethylene- and hypoxia-dependent signalling enables plants to anticipate and prepare for potential flooding-induced hypoxia stress, fine-tune acclimation according to the environmental and internal metabolic context, and effectively orchestrate re-oxygenation responses. Furthermore, plants naturally experience environmental stress manifold throughout their lives, which may lead to long-term morphological adaptations and the encoding of stress memory to promote survival against sequential stressors.

title: Glymphatic Dysfunction as a Multisystem Pathway Linking Systemic Health Conditions to Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms, Risk Factors, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
authors: Abaresh Soroush; Ivantsova Emma; Parmar Mayur S
abstract: The glymphatic system is a glia-associated perivascular pathway involved in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-interstitial fluid (ISF) exchange and the transport and clearance of neurotoxic metabolites, including amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau, from the central nervous system. Growing evidence suggests that alterations in glymphatic and perivascular clearance are associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and may contribute to the accumulation of neurotoxic proteins and neurodegeneration. This review examines the role of the glymphatic system in AD and explores how aging, sleep disturbances, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, high-fat diet, diabetes, and gut microbiome dysbiosis impair glymphatic transport. A recurring mechanism across experimental models is the loss of perivascular AQP4 polarization, while vascular, metabolic, and inflammatory conditions may converge on related perivascular and neurovascular processes that impair CSF-ISF exchange and solute handling. Neuroimaging studies using markers such as DTI-ALPS, perivascular space burden, and free-water measurements provide evidence of alterations in glymphatic-related and perivascular processes in AD and demonstrate associations with amyloid deposition, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline. Furthermore, glymphatic dysfunction may interact with neuroinflammation and tau pathology, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that accelerates disease progression. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including continuous theta-burst stimulation, positive airway pressure therapy for obstructive sleep apnea, pharmacological enhancement of AQP4 function, and nutritional interventions, have shown potential in experimental and early translational studies to influence glymphatic-related processes and may mitigate AD-related pathology. Collectively, current findings suggest that glymphatic and perivascular clearance pathways may represent an important link between systemic health conditions and AD. Because related pathways are implicated across multiple systemic conditions, interventions targeting glymphatic and perivascular dysfunction may have broader relevance to brain health, but their clinical effects remain to be established.

title: DiseaseCIO: a multi-omics atlas for characterizing clinical intervention outcomes across diverse diseases.
authors: Zhai Ruiyang; Ma Te; Su Mu; Wang Hongli; Li Ji et al.
abstract: Heterogeneity in clinical intervention outcomes across patients is a major barrier to precision medicine. The integration of multidimensional high-throughput omics can help reveal the molecular basis of differences in clinical interventions and provide insights into outcome prediction, prognostic stratification, regulatory patterns, and resistance mechanisms. We present DiseaseCIO (Disease Clinical Intervention Outcomes, http://db.edbc.org/DiseaseCIO/), a database that integrates microbiome, transcriptome, and epigenome data with human disease intervention outcomes. It is designed to characterize the molecular landscape associated with disease intervention outcomes at the individual patient level. DiseaseCIO encompasses 42 798 pretreatment samples from 94 disease states, covering 510 treatment regimens involving 377 pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. These samples comprise four types of specimens collected from eight sampling locations. Using the customized iMOD workflow for multi-omics data processing, we generated 20 categories of molecular features and identified >1.84 million candidate feature-outcome associations. DiseaseCIO also provides interactive tools for differential analysis, prognostic evaluation, cross-omics correlation analysis, and cross-cohort integrative analysis of multidimensional features as well as enrichment analysis and signature construction for user-submitted feature sets. DiseaseCIO provides a molecular-level resource for exploring intervention outcome heterogeneity across diseases and identifying candidate multi-omics biomarkers associated with treatment response and prognosis.

title: Pathobiont-directed mucosal immunotherapy targets Ruminococcus gnavus and remodels host-microbiota interactions in colitis.
authors: Wang Zhaoyi; Huang Linlin; Liu Xiaoxia; Cheng Xin; Liang Yuting et al.
abstract: Disease-associated pathobionts are recurrently enriched in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet their causal contribution and selective therapeutic control remain incompletely defined. Here, through clinical microbiome profiling and causal animal studies, we identified Ruminococcus gnavus (Rg) as a key ulcerative colitis (UC)-associated pathobiont whose abundance positively correlates with intestinal oxidative stress and inflammatory levels. To selectively constrain Rg, we engineered CP-EV@Ca, an oral microbiota-directed mucosal immunotherapy that combines pathogen-specific immune targeting with redox modulation. CP-EV@Ca enhanced mucosal antigen presentation, promoted T follicular helper cell-germinal-center B-cell responses and induced robust Rg-specific secretory IgA (sIgA). CP-EV@Ca-induced mucosal immune responses, including enhanced Rg-specific sIgA production, were associated with increased immune coating and reduced Rg expansion. In both acute and chronic colitis models, CP-EV@Ca outperformed 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA), suppressing inflammation and restoring microbial, epithelial and immune homeostasis. These findings demonstrate that pathobiont-specific mucosal immunity can be harnessed to selectively constrain disease-associated bacteria and restore intestinal homeostasis.
